findings.reason: without a followup for §14 nothing schedules the work this revision added, and the open §13 followup misdirects the dispatcher to a done section.
findings.text: `plan-section-declarations` (:23) marks s13 `done`, yet f-cem-004, whose whole body and prompt are `/reckon-build concurrent-edits-meet-at-the-merge §13`, remains `data-status="open"`, and the newly added implementable s14 (:192) has no followup naming it — a coordinator reading the followups dispatches a section that has already landed and never dispatches the one that has not

findings.reason: a base arm whose wait half holds at base makes the node's central contrast unmeasurable and would let the gate pass while the claimed defect is not reproduced.
findings.text: the done-when claims "At the base revision the same test finds the record still present and the wait pending", but `_section_run_unlanded` already skips a discarded run (readiness.py:584 `not _release._discarded(run_id)`, :607) and returns False when no candidate or promotion survives, so the wait half of the base arm cannot fail and the head case's readiness assertion passes on the unfixed code — a record-clearing change would be credited for a release it did not cause

findings.reason: a wrongly attributed consumer sends the node's done-when at a mechanism that never held the wait, and leaves the real one (the landing pass retrying a discarded run's record) unmeasured.
findings.text: the Why attributes the stuck wait to "readiness's `_section_run_unlanded` kept finding that record", but no readiness path reads pending-landing records (readiness.py:535 reads `_ledger_run_rows` and the live pointers, and its only discard test is `promotion.discard_recorded`); the consumers of `pending-landings/` are the landing and recovery paths (pending_landing.finish_pending_landings, pending_landing.py:429, driven by queue_landing.py:1900, and recovery_classification.py:1035) — the actual cost of the stale record after a discard is repeated finish/classify passes, not a held readiness wait

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited anchor resolves: `pending_landing._settled_landing` (reckon/crew/pending_landing.py:119), `pending_landing.clear_pending` (:111), `readiness._section_run_unlanded` (reckon/crew/admission/readiness.py:535), the `crew/pending-landings/` directory (pending_landing.pending_dir, :56), and `crew discard` (promotion.discard, promotion.py:2297).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — s14's base arm asserts the wait stays pending at the base revision, but readiness already skips a discarded run's ledger row, so that half of the base arm cannot reproduce.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — s14 puts every gate log under the run directory, which is durable and openable by a later reader.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers reach the new test filename or the section's prose, and its name states the behaviour.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — s14 blames readiness's `_section_run_unlanded` for finding the pending record, but that function reads the ledger and live pointers only and never reads a pending-landing record, so the stated mechanism does not match the cited consumer.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s14 names one endpoint, "a recorded discard retires the run's pending-landing record"; the no-discard case is a control for that endpoint, not a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — the document marks s13 done but its build followup f-cem-004 stays open, while the newly implementable s14 carries no followup at all.
